name: Feature Engineering Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday feature engineering work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical feature engineering tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday feature engineering work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical feature engineering tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When feature engineering guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. When multiple feature engineering strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
3. Check that feature engineering terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen feature engineering approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. Prefer the simplest feature engineering approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. State assumptions about feature engineering explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
7. Keep feature engineering outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop feature engineering edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of feature engineering correctness.
- Do not skip documenting feature engineering assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for feature engineering, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
